root_cause.text: `mlx4_ib_create_srq()` in the RDMA/mlx4 driver had an incomplete error unwind path, so when `ib_copy_to_udata()` failed after `mlx4_srq_alloc()` had already allocated the SRQ, the code jumped past the SRQ deallocation and leaked the `mlx4_srq` resource.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the failure path from `goto err_wrid;` to `goto err_srq;` and adds `mlx4_srq_free(dev->dev, &srq->msrq);` before the existing cleanup, while the commit message explicitly says `mlx4_srq_alloc() was not undone during error unwind`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the failure path from `goto err_wrid;` to `goto err_srq;` and adds `mlx4_srq_free(dev->dev, &srq->msrq);` before the existing cleanup, while the commit message explicitly says `mlx4_srq_alloc() was not undone during error unwind`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix SRQ resource cleanup on ib_copy_to_udata() failure by freeing the SRQ before unwinding.
intent_record.what: The error path label used after a failed ib_copy_to_udata() call was changed from `err_wrid` to a new `err_srq` label, and a call to `mlx4_srq_free(dev->dev, &srq->msrq);` was inserted at that new label before falling through to `err_wrid`.
intent_record.how: If copying the SRQ number to userspace fails, the code now frees the allocated SRQ before unmapping the user doorbell and returning the error. This prevents the SRQ resource from being leaked on that failure path.

grouping_result.intent: Fix SRQ resource cleanup on ib_copy_to_udata() failure by freeing the SRQ before unwinding.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the incomplete error unwind in mlx4_ib_create_srq() by freeing the allocated SRQ when ib_copy_to_udata() fails, preventing the resource leak.

candidates.rationale: On ib_copy_to_udata() failure, control jumps directly to err_wrid, skipping the SRQ deallocation path after mlx4_srq_alloc() has already succeeded. This incomplete unwind is the leak root cause.
This is the failing operation that triggers the bad error path; when it returns nonzero, the function takes the unwind branch that omits SRQ freeing.
This sets the error status immediately before the incorrect jump, but the bug is that the chosen unwind target does not release the allocated SRQ.

vuln_statements.explanation: This jump sends execution to the wrong unwind label after ib_copy_to_udata() fails, bypassing the SRQ deallocation path even though mlx4_srq_alloc() has already succeeded. That incomplete error unwind is the resource leak root cause.
This is the failure point that triggers the bad unwind path. When this call fails, control enters the branch that incorrectly skips freeing the allocated SRQ.
This error assignment precedes the incorrect jump, but by itself is not the defect; together with the bad target it leads to unwinding without releasing the already-allocated SRQ.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this version of mlx4_ib_create_srq(). In the user-object path, after successful `mlx4_srq_alloc(...)`, the code does `if (ib_copy_to_udata(...)) { err = -EFAULT; goto err_wrid; }`. The `err_wrid` label unwinds the SRQ allocation by calling `mlx4_ib_db_unmap_user(...)` or `kfree(srq->wrid)`, then `mlx4_mtt_cleanup(...)`, buffer/umem cleanup, and finally `kfree(srq)`. This means the error path does not jump past SRQ deallocation; the allocated SRQ is cleaned up. Since the problematic incomplete unwind path is absent here, `has_bug` is false and there is no fix to detect within this snippet because the bug is not present.
